posts.caption:
Your dog's nose has up to 300 million scent receptors. Yours has about 6 million.

So a new place is big news for them. There is so much to smell.

That is one reason we take introductions slowly. New guests get time to sniff and settle in.

posts.angle: Body language cheat sheet. Save and share bait. Shows we read dogs for a living.

slides.title: Your dog is talking *all day.*
slides.sub: Here is how to listen. Save this one.

slides.title: The play bow
slides.body: Front legs down. Rear end up. It means: let's play.

slides.title: The yawn
slides.body: Not always sleepy. A yawn can be a sign your dog feels stressed.

slides.title: The wag
slides.body: A wagging tail does not always mean happy. Look at the whole body.

slides.title: Whale eye
slides.body: You can see the white of the eye. Your dog may feel uneasy. Give them space.

slides.title: The wiggle
slides.body: Loose body. Soft face. Wiggly walk. That is a relaxed dog.

slides.title: Reading dogs is our *job.*
slides.body: It is how we match dogs for group play. Share this with everyone who cares for your dog.

posts.caption:
Your dog talks all day. Just not with words.

A play bow means let's play.
A yawn can mean stress, not sleep.
A wag does not always mean happy.
Whale eye means give some space.
A loose, wiggly body means relaxed.

Reading these signs is our job. It is how we match dogs for group play.

Save this. Share it with everyone who cares for your dog.

Source: American Kennel Club

posts.angle: Weekend share bait. Four facts that sound fake.

slides.title: Nose prints are like fingerprints.
slides.body: No two dogs have the same nose print.

slides.title: Dogs sweat through their paws.
slides.body: Their paw pads have sweat glands. Most cooling comes from panting.

slides.title: Dogs see color.
slides.body: Just not like us. They see mostly blue and yellow. Red looks dull.

slides.title: Dogs likely dream.
slides.body: Twitching paws during sleep? Experts think they may be dreaming.

slides.title: 225 families reviewed us on *Google.*
slides.body: Read what they say. Then tell us about your dog.

posts.caption:
